text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Senior members of the Welfare Party have benefitted enormously from the party, through tenders and contracts handed out to Welfare-run companies by Welfare-run municipalities.
- A letter from the IMF to economy minister Gunes Taner says that the fund approves of the government's program and is ready to provide support.
- More than 2,000 people died in crashes on Turkish roads in the first six months of 1997,
- A price war among private hospitals and clinics has health professionals concerned that quality of treatment may suffer.
- The government's target is to raise the price of petrol to the equivalent of one dollar (TL 164,000).
- Teaching unions back the government's secularist education reforms.
- Turkey is determined to take action to prevent money laundering ahead of an OECD meeting in Paris in September.
- There are more mosques in Istanbul than primary schools.
- Turkey is setting up special police teams to combat fraud and money laundering.
- The income from the government's price rises exceeds the cost of the new education reforms.
- Last year the northern Iraqi Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and Turkey's Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) were close. Now the KDP is raining insults on the PKK.
